chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The thief is not cut (amputated) during a year of drought/famine with regard to everything that is eaten, such as bread and meat, and similar to that.
ai.seo_question: When is the punishment of hand amputation for theft suspended in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of *raf' al-hajr* (removal of punishment) during famine, emphasizing that the threshold for hand amputation is suspended to preserve life when basic sustenance is scarce. Scholars note that this ruling applies broadly to all consumable food items, not merely the primary staple, reflecting the juristic priority of *darar* (harm) over *hudud* (fixed punishments). This aligns with the Shia emphasis on the flexibility of legal rulings in response to changing social and economic conditions.
